Stamp: DESIGNED    Source: [V10 §7E-TSC / 1. What TSC Is and Is Not] [MAP C-TSC]

ALONE
- What it is: DESIGNED — An organized holding mode inside the unified Catalog pre-ingest store for one real conversation. The structural database and the pre-ingest payload records are two aspects of that same holding system. [V10 §7E-TSC / 1. What TSC Is and Is Not]
- Takes in: DESIGNED — Third-party contributions, Ness's contributions, N.H outputs, links to held BOP observation captures and references to SIA assessment events; every session item begins with `pending_fingerprint_authorization`. [V10 §7E-TSC / 2. Relationship to §7E] [V10 §7E-TSC / 9. BOP and SIA Event-Link Handling] [V10 §7E-TSC / 10. N.H Output Preservation]
- Does: DESIGNED — Preserves conversation order, separate speaker streams, attribution certainty and branch relationships; seals a completed or interrupted conversation; waits for session-specific authorization; then lets eligible items progress through the normal Catalog root-ingestion path. [V10 §7E-TSC / 2. Relationship to §7E] [V10 §7E-TSC / 13. Normal Session Close and Sealing] [V10 §7E-TSC / 14. Interrupted-Session Sealing and Linked Continuation Caches] [V10 §7E-TSC / 17. Exact Promotion Sequence]
- Gives out: DESIGNED — Promoted-root identifiers linked to preserved session provenance, plus a frozen encrypted read-only retained structural archive after every item resolves. [V10 §7E-TSC / 5. Contribution Record Schema] [V10 §7E-TSC / 17. Exact Promotion Sequence] [V10 §7E-TSC / 23. Post-Promotion Retained Safety Archive]
- Must never: DESIGNED — Become another memory or Meaning Engine; interpret session material; bypass Catalog; call `append_root()` directly; add fields to the sealed seven-field root; promote an unresolved speaker; convert a third party's statement into a fact about Ness; merge streams; destroy material; reconstruct uncaptured material; reopen captured contents of a sealed session; expose a sealed cache or retained archive for human inspection; or resubmit the archive as ordinary evidence. [V10 §7E-TSC / 30. Explicit Prohibited Behaviors]
- Fails closed by: DESIGNED — Leaves an unauthorized session waiting; prevents a start with missing or stale SACL; pauses an already-authorized promotion while security conditions are absent; halts on database-integrity failure; seals an unknown readable startup state as interrupted; and denies archive access outside bounded machine-level integrity or recovery uses. [V10 §7E-TSC / 16. Fingerprint Authorization Through BAI and SACL] [V10 §7E-TSC / 28. Fail-Closed Behavior]

### C-TSC.1 — Session holding boundary
Stamp: DESIGNED    Source: [V10 §7E-TSC / 1. What TSC Is and Is Not]

ALONE
- What it is: DESIGNED — The provenance boundary holding a faithful conversation record until its material can traverse Catalog and the Meaning Engine. [V10 §7E-TSC / 1. What TSC Is and Is Not]
- Takes in: DESIGNED — Captured session material already resident in Catalog pre-ingest. [V10 §7E-TSC / 1. What TSC Is and Is Not]
- Does: DESIGNED — Organizes sessions, contributions, participants, branches, blockers and lifecycle records around the shared pre-ingest items. [V10 §7E-TSC / 1. What TSC Is and Is Not]
- Gives out: DESIGNED — A coherent held session whose material must undergo the full Catalog-to-Meaning-Engine path before influencing output. [V10 §7E-TSC / 1. What TSC Is and Is Not]
- Must never: DESIGNED — Create a separate upstream cache, second long-term memory, semantic interpretation store, independent route into readings or Person-Boxes, identity fusion, or facts about Ness from another person's statements. [V10 §7E-TSC / 1. What TSC Is and Is Not]
- Fails closed by: DESIGNED — Keeps held material unavailable to downstream components until its governing authorization and Catalog blockers clear. [V10 §0B / ACCESS AND AUTHORIZATION BOUNDARY]

### C-TSC.2 — Shared Catalog holding
Stamp: DESIGNED    Source: [V10 §7E-TSC / 2. Relationship to §7E]

ALONE
- What it is: DESIGNED — One added blocker type and a session organization layer within the existing Catalog holding system. [V10 §7E-TSC / 2. Relationship to §7E]
- Takes in: DESIGNED — Catalog records containing `capture_id`, raw payload, capture timestamp, front-door type, source metadata, proposed catalog fields, blockers, resolution history, lifecycle state and a resulting `root_id` when promoted. [V10 §7E-TSC / 2. Relationship to §7E]
- Does: DESIGNED — Adds `pending_fingerprint_authorization` alongside blockers such as `speaker_unresolved` and `thread_unresolved`; relates items by session, sequence, participant, attribution, branch, BOP/SIA links, output and lifecycle history. [V10 §7E-TSC / 2. Relationship to §7E]
- Gives out: DESIGNED — After session authorization, items with no remaining blockers follow `held` → `ready` → `promoting` → `promoted`; the structural record retains the root identifier and the Catalog record remains as provenance. [V10 §7E-TSC / 2. Relationship to §7E]
- Must never: DESIGNED — Put raw payloads in the structural database, send conversation or BOP captures to long-term roots while authorization is pending, silently delete blocked material, or let one blocked item prevent unrelated ready items from progressing. [V10 §7E-TSC / 2. Relationship to §7E]
- Fails closed by: DESIGNED — Holds blocked items indefinitely and keeps them invisible to the Meaning Engine until the governing blockers clear. [V10 §7E-TSC / 2. Relationship to §7E]

### C-TSC.3 — Transactional structural store
Stamp: DESIGNED    Source: [V10 §7E-TSC / 3. Transactional Database Model]

ALONE
- What it is: DESIGNED — A local transactional store for session organization, requiring ACID transactions, crash-safe writes, local-only operation and no network dependency. [V10 §7E-TSC / 3. Transactional Database Model]
- What it is: ACCEPTED — SQLite with one self-contained local database file per session; exact version, journal/WAL mode, synchronous settings, page/cache tuning, encryption library/mode and file layout remain unspecified. [04/NH_B15_TSC_TRANSACTIONAL_STORE_ARCHITECTURE_v1_4_CANDIDATE.md §3]
- Takes in: DESIGNED — Structural rows in `sessions`, `contributions`, `participants`, `attribution_assessments`, `branch_links`, `bop_preingest_links`, `sia_event_links`, `nh_outputs`, `blockers`, `blocker_history`, `lifecycle_events`, `promotion_state` and `security_audit_refs`. [V10 §7E-TSC / 3. Transactional Database Model]
- Does: ACCEPTED — Serializes all writes through one owning process per session; commits state changes with their history, enforces foreign keys and uniqueness, and maintains one shared monotonic allocator for contribution and output order. ### C-TSC.14.2 — Continuation creation
Stamp: DESIGNED    Source: [V10 §7E-TSC / 14. Interrupted-Session Sealing and Linked Continuation Caches]
ALONE
- What it is: DESIGNED — A new session for conversation resumed after an interrupted unit. [V10 §7E-TSC / 14. Interrupted-Session Sealing and Linked Continuation Caches]
- Takes in: ACCEPTED — C9 request: `interrupted_session_id`, durable `resume_event_id`; the coordinator owns creation and B15 owns both stores. [04/NH_B_INT_4_TSC_AUTHORIZATION_PROMOTION_AND_INTERRUPTED_CONTINUATION_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §7]
- Does: ACCEPTED — Creates a new `session_id` and separate B15 database, records `continuation_of_session_id`, `tsc_session_created` and `cache_interrupted_linked`; the new session remains mutable until it is itself sealed. [04/NH_B_INT_4_TSC_AUTHORIZATION_PROMOTION_AND_INTERRUPTED_CONTINUATION_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §6]
- Gives out: DESIGNED — A separate continuation authorized and promoted independently. [V10 §7E-TSC / 14. Interrupted-Session Sealing and Linked Continuation Caches]
- Gives out: ACCEPTED — C9 response: `new_session_id`, `continuation_of_session_id`, `link_ref`. [04/NH_B_INT_4_TSC_AUTHORIZATION_PROMOTION_AND_INTERRUPTED_CONTINUATION_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §7]
- Must never: ACCEPTED — Combine the databases or transfer mutable state, content, authority, blockers, retry state or promotion checkpoints; the link is provenance only. [04/NH_B_INT_4_TSC_AUTHORIZATION_PROMOTION_AND_INTERRUPTED_CONTINUATION_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §6] [04/NH_B_INT_4_TSC_AUTHORIZATION_PROMOTION_AND_INTERRUPTED_CONTINUATION_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §7]
- Fails closed by: ACCEPTED — An identity conflict prevents session creation and is recorded; replay of the same resume event finds the existing continuation rather than creating another. [04/NH_B_INT_4_TSC_AUTHORIZATION_PROMOTION_AND_INTERRUPTED_CONTINUATION_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §6] [04/NH_B_INT_4_TSC_AUTHORIZATION_PROMOTION_AND_INTERRUPTED_CONTINUATION_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §7]

- Gives out: ACCEPTED — Exactly one authorized session and one durable receipt for its successful authorization, with promotion as a separate resumable phase. ### C-TSC.16.4 — Authorization claim record
Stamp: ACCEPTED    Source: [04/NH_B_INT_4_TSC_AUTHORIZATION_PROMOTION_AND_INTERRUPTED_CONTINUATION_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §8]
ALONE
- What it is: ACCEPTED — Proposed `tsc_authorization_claim`, the session-purpose serialization slot; it grants no authority. [04/NH_B_INT_4_TSC_AUTHORIZATION_PROMOTION_AND_INTERRUPTED_CONTINUATION_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §8]
- Takes in: ACCEPTED — Required unique `authorization_claim_id` [proposed]; required `session_id`; required `purpose = tsc_promotion:<session_id>`; required current `state`; `attached_authorization_operation_id` required from A1; `durable_receipt_ref` required from A2; optional `supersedes_claim_ref`, `superseded_by_claim_ref` and `terminal_at`; `created_at`; and the common `schema_version`/optional `supersedes_ref`. [04/NH_B_INT_4_TSC_AUTHORIZATION_PROMOTION_AND_INTERRUPTED_CONTINUATION_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §8]
- Does: ACCEPTED — Enforces at most one active-or-successful claim per `(session_id, purpose)`; permits only its attached token to be consumed. State vocabulary is `claimed`, `consumed_pending_commit`, `authorized_complete`, `released`, `superseded`, `failed`. [04/NH_B_INT_4_TSC_AUTHORIZATION_PROMOTION_AND_INTERRUPTED_CONTINUATION_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §8]
- Gives out: ACCEPTED — The single operation that owns the attempt, plus explicit append-only release or supersession links. [04/NH_B_INT_4_TSC_AUTHORIZATION_PROMOTION_AND_INTERRUPTED_CONTINUATION_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §8]
- Must never: ACCEPTED — Authorize a different session, substitute for the durable receipt, permit two successful receipts, or replace a durably consumed token by consuming another for the same authority. Replacement is allowed only after the old operation is durably terminal before consumption or its unconsumed token is revoked and its claim safely superseded. [04/NH_B_INT_4_TSC_AUTHORIZATION_PROMOTION_AND_INTERRUPTED_CONTINUATION_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §8]
- Fails closed by: ACCEPTED — A concurrent loser returns the existing authorization reference or fails closed. Without a verified receipt the old operation becomes `failed`; the old claim is explicitly released/superseded before a new claim may win with a new token and operation. [04/NH_B_INT_4_TSC_AUTHORIZATION_PROMOTION_AND_INTERRUPTED_CONTINUATION_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §8]

### C-TSC.17 — Ordered promotion
Stamp: DESIGNED    Source: [V10 §7E-TSC / 17. Exact Promotion Sequence]

ALONE
- What it is: DESIGNED — A three-phase process: pre-promotion checks, ordered per-item promotion, and a completion/archive gate. [V10 §7E-TSC / 17. Exact Promotion Sequence]
- Takes in: DESIGNED — An authorized session, current security conditions, privacy classifications, blockers and the captured session ordering. [V10 §7E-TSC / 17. Exact Promotion Sequence]
- Does: DESIGNED — Verifies authorization and non-stale BAI/SACL conditions; applies privacy decisions; marks exclusions and transfers their raw content to sealed protected storage; makes otherwise unblocked items ready; keeps non-fingerprint blockers; enters `promoting`, timestamps the start and writes `cache_promotion_started`. [V10 §7E-TSC / 17. Exact Promotion Sequence]
- Does: DESIGNED — In ascending session order, skips recorded exclusions, defers blocked items with a pending-blocked checkpoint, and promotes ready items. An existing `promoted_root_id` is reused. Otherwise the fingerprint blocker clears, session context enters Catalog `source_metadata`, Catalog validates the envelope and remaining blockers, and its normal writer route appends the root. Success commits the resulting root identifier and promoted item state. BOP captures interleave by `occurred_at`. [V10 §7E-TSC / 17. Exact Promotion Sequence]
- Gives out: DESIGNED — Only when every item is promoted or excluded with no unresolved failure: `promoted`, `promotion_completed_at`, `cache_promotion_completed`, then a verified retained archive, `tsc_retained_archive_created` and `archived`. [V10 §7E-TSC / 17. Exact Promotion Sequence]
- Must never: DESIGNED — Record completion, create the retained archive or enter `promoted`/`archived` while any item is blocked; demand a new fingerprint when non-fingerprint blockers clear; put `promotion_failed` in an item lifecycle; or add session metadata to the root schema. [V10 §7E-TSC / 17. Exact Promotion Sequence]
- Fails closed by: DESIGNED — A blocked item remains pending and resumes automatically when its blocker clears. A recorded item failure preventing completion sets the session to `promotion_failed`, writes `cache_promotion_failed` and sends the private notice; the failure class controls the next retry action. [V10 §7E-TSC / 17. Exact Promotion Sequence]

### C-TSC.20 — Automatic retry
Stamp: DESIGNED    Source: [V10 §7E-TSC / 20. Automatic Retry Rules]

ALONE
- What it is: DESIGNED — Three distinct retry/authorization cases: A, continuation of already-authorized interrupted promotion; B, genuinely new promotion authorization; C, temporary technical-failure retry. [V10 §7E-TSC / 20. Automatic Retry Rules]
- Takes in: DESIGNED — Existing authorization, the recorded failure class, remaining retry allowance, declared backoff and current security conditions. [V10 §7E-TSC / 20. Automatic Retry Rules]
- Does: DESIGNED — In A, resumes automatically after security checks and pauses if recognized-Ness conditions are absent. In B, requires new authorization only if the session was never authorized or the original token was revoked before promotion began. In C, retries temporary retryable failures automatically after bounded backoff, checks security, changes `promotion_failed` to `promoting` and resumes the failed items. [V10 §7E-TSC / 20. Automatic Retry Rules]
- Gives out: DESIGNED — Automatic continuation where eligible, a security pause until conditions recover, or a session remaining `promotion_failed` when attempts are exhausted or failure is non-retryable. [V10 §7E-TSC / 20. Automatic Retry Rules]
- Must never: DESIGNED — Require a new fingerprint or manual SACL confirmation for continuation of valid already-authorized promotion, silently reuse expired authorization, or treat a request for another attempt as biometric authorization. [V10 §7E-TSC / 20. Automatic Retry Rules] [V10 §7E-TSC / 30. Explicit Prohibited Behaviors]
- Fails closed by: DESIGNED — Keeps the failed state on exhaustion/non-retryable failure; sends a private session-specific notice without content, indicating that another attempt may be requested. A requested attempt for an already-authorized session checks security before returning to `promoting`; it needs no new fingerprint unless case B applies. [V10 §7E-TSC / 20. Automatic Retry Rules]

### C-TSC.27 — Startup recovery
Stamp: DESIGNED    Source: [V10 §7E-TSC / 27. Startup Recovery and Crash Recovery]

ALONE
- What it is: DESIGNED — Examination of every session database at startup, acting only on committed state. [V10 §7E-TSC / 27. Startup Recovery and Crash Recovery]
- Takes in: DESIGNED — Session lifecycle, item progress and existing archive state. [V10 §7E-TSC / 27. Startup Recovery and Crash Recovery]
- Does: DESIGNED — Seals `active` as `interrupted` with `cache_sealed`/`interrupted_crash`; resumes `promoting` automatically after security checks; starts promotion from `authorized`; leaves `sealed` and `interrupted` waiting. From `promotion_failed`, inspects the failure class and retries temporary retryable failures with attempts remaining after backoff/security checks; exhausted or non-retryable failures remain failed pending a requested attempt. [V10 §7E-TSC / 27. Startup Recovery and Crash Recovery]
- Does: DESIGNED — From `promoted`, creates the missing archive and enters `archived`, or repairs the lifecycle idempotently when a successful archive already exists. `archived` and `permanently_sealed` are terminal states requiring no ordinary runtime action. [V10 §7E-TSC / 27. Startup Recovery and Crash Recovery]
- Gives out: DESIGNED — Preserved committed material and resumed eligible work without duplication; an uncommitted write is absent. [V10 §7E-TSC / 27. Startup Recovery and Crash Recovery]
- Must never: DESIGNED — Reconstruct uncommitted material, repeat promoted work, require a new fingerprint for a completed archive transition, or expose terminal archives to ordinary operation. [V10 §7E-TSC / 27. Startup Recovery and Crash Recovery] [V10 §7E-TSC / 30. Explicit Prohibited Behaviors]
- Fails closed by: ACCEPTED — Structural corruption triggers read-only quarantine, a failure record, no promotion and honest notification; readable unknown lifecycle state is sealed as interrupted. [04/NH_B15_TSC_TRANSACTIONAL_STORE_ARCHITECTURE_v1_4_CANDIDATE.md §9]

Fail-Closed Behavior]

## Scope and path placement

C-TSC's decided segment belongs to CY-D — Third-party session → TSC → promotion and to P-MAIN's TSC-held branch into CY-D. These are local use placements; they do not change CH00's complete-path stamps or supply its missing end-to-end steps. The recursive sub-part inventory places each card within that session path. CH11 owns the assembled side-path template.

The source-defined phases remain separate: receipt-backed authorization, then automatic ordered promotion. B15 owns structural session/item state; Catalog owns payload and intake; BAI owns token consumption; SACL owns recognition/freshness; the privacy owner decides exclusion. No runtime implementation, source promotion, new schema activation or modification of earlier chapters is implied.

## Explicit remaining scope

- CH05-a and CH05-d own the general B9 retry machinery, timeout/backoff values and reread orchestration. This piece preserves TSC's A/B/C retry distinctions without assigning Bundle 6 values to an unrelated operation class.
- CH08-a owns full privacy/protected-storage mechanics. TSC's actual exclusion outcomes, opaque references and recovery boundaries are included here; TSC does not take that decision authority.
- CH08-d owns full BOP capture/observation mechanics; CH09-c, CH09-d and CH09-e own complete SIA, SACL and BAI internals. Their TSC request/response contents and exact authorization conditions are included here.
- CH11 owns the complete CY-D side-path assembly. CH12-a and CH12-d regenerate all gap and conflict entries from the finished chapters after audit fixes.
- B15's implementation choices and B-INT-4's implementation technology remain the open slots below. No new engine, timeout, encoding or field name is selected to fill them.

## Review of plain gates and empty boxes

The remaining plain gates state actual own-operation prerequisites, a person's request, or the separately owned seal authorization whose more exact owner is not specified. They do not substitute a step's action for a gate. The per-card gate inventory below identifies every retained plain line.

The whole-card scan considered all ALONE and TOGETHER fields and every USED BY cell. Record-member types and names do not imply an invented independent runtime failure mechanism. A condition check is not gated by its own successful result; token and integrity condition cards therefore retain an empty Gated by box where the source supplies no additional gate. Field references to a consumer's gate are not themselves a second gate on storing that field. A refusal-reason field describes a refusal; it does not own a new refusal operation.

The review filled the seal-timestamp atomic prohibition, required-audit-write failure on audit references and coordination-duplicate records, and the explicit authoritative-state fallback for a missing/stale promotion-pass summary. Existing technical failure, authority, privacy, archive and ownership outcomes remain in their owning cards. In particular, a third party's storage request has no independent failure mechanism, and an archive-location reference creates no independent archive-access operation.

No active behavior is stamped BUILT except the link to the already-built seven-field root schema. The source-defined field/state/event names remain literal; proposed and B15 design-level records retain those qualifiers. The source name scan treats quotation marks around enum values and expanded request/response object notation as notation, not different names. Historical source-artifact names and the historical embedded-design fingerprint are provenance, not missing runtime fields; `cache_promotion_*` is a collective event pattern represented by the individual active events.

| C-TSC.3.4 | Gated by | ACCEPTED — The previous owner must be provably gone before hand-off to a replacement owner. [04/NH_B15_TSC_TRANSACTIONAL_STORE_ARCHITECTURE_v1_4_CANDIDATE.md §7] | Own hand-off prerequisite: evidence that the previous process owner is gone; no separate ownership mechanism is invented. |
| C-TSC.13.2 | Gated by | DESIGNED — Normal session closure is occurring. [V10 §7E-TSC / 13. Normal Session Close and Sealing] | Own event precondition: this held-or-blocked condition is applied at normal close. |
| C-TSC.16.3.1 | Gated by | ACCEPTED — The §25 authorization boundary governs access to coordination records. [04/NH_B_INT_4_TSC_AUTHORIZATION_PROMOTION_AND_INTERRUPTED_CONTINUATION_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §8] | Outside governing authorization boundary: the source refers to §25 collectively and does not assign this record-access decision to a more specific TSC card. |
| C-TSC.16.4.7 | Gated by | ACCEPTED — Replacement requires the earlier operation terminal before consumption, or its unconsumed token revoked and claim safely superseded. [04/NH_B_INT_4_TSC_AUTHORIZATION_PROMOTION_AND_INTERRUPTED_CONTINUATION_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §8] | Own supersession-reference precondition: the prior operation must be terminal before consumption or safely superseded after revocation. |
| C-TSC.16.4.8 | Gated by | ACCEPTED — A durably consumed token cannot be replaced by another token for the same authorization. [04/NH_B_INT_4_TSC_AUTHORIZATION_PROMOTION_AND_INTERRUPTED_CONTINUATION_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §8] | Own replacement-reference constraint: durable consumption prohibits another token for the same authorization. |
| C-TSC.20.3 | Gated by | DESIGNED — The failure is temporary and retryable, the declared backoff has elapsed and attempts remain within the bounded maximum. [V10 §7E-TSC / 20. | C-TSC.20.4 | Gated by | DESIGNED — Ness requests another attempt after automatic retries exhaust or the failure is non-retryable. [V10 §7E-TSC / 20. Automatic Retry Rules] | A person’s request for another attempt, explicitly distinct from biometric authorization. |
| C-TSC.23.1 | Gated by | ACCEPTED — The created snapshot must verify before the final `archived` commit. [04/NH_B15_TSC_TRANSACTIONAL_STORE_ARCHITECTURE_v1_4_CANDIDATE.md §8] | Own final-commit prerequisite: the created snapshot must verify. |
| C-TSC.23.2.4 | Gated by | ACCEPTED — Snapshot integrity must verify before the hash is treated as authoritative evidence. [04/NH_B15_TSC_TRANSACTIONAL_STORE_ARCHITECTURE_v1_4_CANDIDATE.md §9] | Own evidential precondition: the snapshot hash is authoritative only after verification. |
| C-TSC.23.6.1 | Gated by | ACCEPTED — Separate permanent-seal authorization must remain valid under its owning authority. [04/NH_B15_TSC_TRANSACTIONAL_STORE_ARCHITECTURE_v1_4_CANDIDATE.md §9] | Separate external authority: the source requires its validity but does not specify a more exact owner; the gap remains explicit. |
| C-TSC.23.9 | Gated by | DESIGNED — The access purpose must be a permitted machine-level function without human disclosure or ordinary reasoning use. [V10 §7E-TSC / 28. Fail-Closed Behavior] | Own access-purpose restriction: only the stated machine-level functions without human or ordinary-reasoning disclosure. |
| C-TSC.28.6 | Gated by | ACCEPTED — The actual authority owner must be available to provide the required decision. [04/NH_B_INT_4_TSC_AUTHORIZATION_PROMOTION_AND_INTERRUPTED_CONTINUATION_WIRING_v1_3_CANDIDATE.md §10] | Outside decision-owner availability: the relevant owner varies with the requested authority; TSC cannot substitute a decision. |
